tests: junit:docs/evidence/S1/junit/host-vitest.xml::auditStorageSnapshot — allow-list judgment (A15) > negative control: a seeded leak in every storage kind is detected
A15.notes: After every flow (uc01, uc05, uc07, uc10, uc11, the eval runs, and a full pick→edit→share→copy→export flow) the audit finds zero allow-list violations: no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/Cache Storage/cookies at all, no post text in storage, URL, referrer, console output or any network request, and every request is same-origin. The seeded-leak negative control proves the audit detects violations (and this is real: the audit caught tesseract.js persisting traineddata into an IndexedDB 'keyval-store' on the first run — fixed with cacheMethod 'none', see metrics.md).

limitations: The OS share sheet itself is not automatable; navigator.share is spied and its payload asserted. Real-device share/installed-PWA/clipboard behavior remains NOT_RUN (A27/A30).

Playwright's WebKit on Linux cannot grant clipboard permissions; readText is platform-denied there. Copy is verified in WebKit via a real paste round-trip, and by a real granted clipboard read in Chromium.
WebKit-on-Linux is not iOS Safari; no real-device claim is made anywhere.

The language gate is a deterministic script + common-English-word ratio measured on the 21 readable synthetic fixtures (100% English accepted, 0% non-English accepted, threshold centered in the measured gap); it does not prove behavior on arbitrary real-world posts, and list-style English posts sit closer to the threshold (min 0.175 vs threshold 0.12) than prose posts.

Cleanup is deterministic English-only rules; the model cleanup and its browser eval over every variant fixture is S4 (A19). The S1 browser eval covers the 12-fixture standard set; variant fixtures are proven exact host-side on gold input and exercised end-to-end by the uc10/uc11 flows.

longpost01's measured chrome leakage 0.111 is a single-digit tokenizer artifact of the list marker ('5.' in gold vs '5,' in OCR), not surviving UI chrome; the mean leakage is 0.009 (bar 2%). See metrics.md.

The A15 audits prove the flows that ran, in Chromium and WebKit on this machine: no storage beyond the allow-list existed (S1 allows none at all), no post text in storage, URL, cookies, console or network, all requests same-origin. They do not prove arbitrary user behavior. tesseract.js no longer persists traineddata (cacheMethod 'none'); the 2 MB pinned file is re-fetched same-origin per fresh session until the S2 service-worker app shell precaches /ocr-assets/.
Where a browser build lacks IndexedDB enumeration (databases()), the audit records a note instead of silently passing; both engines used here enumerate it.
A14 (zero network requests after the model is cached) is S3; S1's request audit asserts no post text in any request and same-origin-only traffic.
